subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I can say twelve personality adjectives like shy, kind, polite and tidy.
I can match adjectives to their opposites and notice the prefix un-.
I can say what personality a job needs: In my job, I need to be kind.

tf.s: The opposite of shy is confident.
tf.why: Yes! Shy and confident are opposites.

tf.s: The opposite of kind is polite.
tf.why: The opposite of kind is mean. Polite and rude are a pair.

tf.s: We add un- to friendly to make its opposite.
A polite person always says please and thank you.
tf.why: Yes! That is what polite people do.

tf.s: A lazy person works a lot and never stops.
tf.why: That is a hard-working person. A lazy person doesn't like to work.

tf.s: The opposite of polite is rude.
tf.why: Great! Polite and rude are opposites.

tf.s: A tidy person has got all their things in a mess.
tf.why: A tidy person has got all their things in order.

tf.s: A shy person is afraid to talk to new people.
tf.why: Yes! That is the meaning of shy.
Mean is negative; kind is its positive opposite.

tf.s: We make the opposite of tidy with the prefix dis-.

boxes.q: What is the opposite of tidy?
What is the opposite of lazy?
"She's afraid to talk to new people." She is ___.
boxes.why: A shy person is afraid to talk to new people.
Kind is a nice thing to be.

boxes.q: Which prefix makes the opposite of friendly?
In my job, I need ___ kind.
boxes.why: The structure is I need to be + adjective.

boxes.q: A person who doesn't share and is not nice is ___.
boxes.why: Mean is the opposite of kind.

boxes.q: Which adjective is NOT made with un-?
boxes.why: Rude is a different word; it is the opposite of polite.

boxes.q: A person who talks easily on a stage is ___.
boxes.why: Confident people are not afraid in front of others.

boxes.q: Which adjective describes someone who is not nice to new people?
boxes.why: Unfriendly is the opposite of friendly.

hunt.q: All her things are in order.

mcq.q: Which list has three opposite pairs?
o: shy – confident, kind – mean, polite – rude
shy – kind, lazy – tidy, rude – mean
tidy – polite, kind – confident, lazy – shy
rude – mean, shy – lazy, kind – tidy
mcq.why: These are the lesson's opposite pairs.

mcq.q: Which two adjectives use the prefix un- to make their opposites?
What is the lesson's tip for learning a new word?
mcq.why: Thinking of the opposite helps you learn new adjectives.

mcq.q: Which word is a personality adjective?
mcq.why: Curly, tall and fair are about appearance, not personality.

mcq.q: "I'm a doctor. In my job, I need to be ___." Which is best?
mcq.why: A doctor helps sick people, so kind and hard-working fit.

mcq.q: Write a definition for a guessing game: hard-working.
o: He works a lot and never stops until he finishes.
He is afraid of new people.
mcq.why: A hard-working person works a lot.

mcq.q: Ahmed leaves his books and clothes everywhere. What is he?
Why does a waiter need to be polite and friendly?
o: He talks to many customers every day.
mcq.why: Waiters meet many people, so they need to be nice to them.

mcq.q: Is "mean" made with un-, and what is its opposite?
mcq.why: Mean is its own word; its opposite is kind.

mcq.q: Which sentence describes a classmate in a positive way?
o: My friend Salim is very kind and hard-working.
My friend Salim is lazy and untidy.
mcq.why: Kind and hard-working are positive adjectives.
